Some(\"claude-print\".to_string())\n228\t/// );\n229\t///\n230\t/// // Second rule (catch-all) matches.\n231\t/// assert_eq!(\n232\t///     match_adapter(\"other-model\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n233\t///     Some(\"default-adapter\".to_string())\n234\t/// );\n235\t/// ```\n236\tpub fn match_adapter(model: &str, rules: &[RoutingRule], default: &str) -> Option<String> {\n237\t    // Compile rules and test in order (first match wins).\n238\t    for rule in rules {\n239\t        match CompiledRule::from_rule(rule) {\n240\t            Ok(compiled) => {\n241\t                if compiled.matches(model) {\n242\t                    return Some(compiled.adapter.clone());\n243\t                }\n244\t            }\n245\t            Err(e) => {\n246\t                // Log the error but continue with other rules.\n247\t                // Invalid patterns are skipped rather than failing the entire dispatch.\n248\t                tracing::warn!(\n249\t                    pattern = %rule.match_model,\n250\t                    error = %e,\n251\t                    \"invalid routing pattern — skipping rule\"\n252\t                );\n253\t            }\n254\t        }\n255\t    }\n256\t\n257\t    // No rule matched — use default if provided.\n258\t    if default.is_empty() {\n259\t        None\n260\t    } else {\n261\t        Some(default.to_string())\n262\t    }\n263\t}\n264\t\n265\t/// Match a model name against a single glob pattern using the glob crate.\n266\t///\n267\t/// This is a lower-level function that tests if a glob pattern matches a model name.\n268\t/// It uses the `glob` crate's Pattern type directly for glob-style pattern matching.\n269\t///\n270\t/// # Arguments\n271\t///\n272\t/// * `pattern` - Glob pattern to match (e.g., \"claude-*\", \"gpt-*\", \"*\").\n273\t/// * `model_name` - The model name to test against the pattern.\n274\t///\n275\t/// # Returns\n276\t///\n277\t/// * `Some(())` - The pattern matches the model name.\n278\t/// * `None` - The pattern does not match or is invalid.\n279\t///\n280\t/// # Edge Cases\n281\t///\n282\t/// * Empty pattern: Returns `None` (no match).\n283\t/// * Empty model name: Returns `None` (no match).\n284\t/// * Invalid glob pattern: Returns `None` (no match).\n285\t///\n286\t/// # Glob Pattern Syntax\n287\t///\n288\t/// * `*` - Matches any sequence of non-separator characters.\n289\t/// * `**` - Matches any sequence of characters, including path separators.\n290\t/// * `?` - Matches any single non-separator character.\n291\t/// * `[a-z]` - Matches any character in the bracket.\n292\t/// * `[!a-z]` - Matches any character not in the bracket.\n293\t///\n294\t/// # Examples\n295\t///\n296\t/// ```\n297\t/// use needle::routing::match_adapter_with_glob;\n298\t///\n299\t/// // Match with wildcard\n300\t/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"claude-sonnet-4-6\").is_some());\n301\t/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"claude-opus-4-6\").is_some());\n302\t/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"gpt-4\").is_none());\n303\t///\n304\t/// // Match with double wildcard\n305\t/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"**\", \"any-model\").is_some());\n306\t///\n307\t/// // Edge cases\n308\t/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"\", \"model\").is_none());\n309\t/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"pattern\", \"\").is_none());\n310\t/// ```\n311\tpub fn match_adapter_with_glob(pattern: &str, model_name: &str) -> Option<()> {\n312\t    // Handle edge cases\n313\t    if pattern.is_empty() || model_name.is_empty() {\n314\t        return None;\n315\t    }\n316\t\n317\t    // Use the glob crate to compile and match the pattern\n318\t    match glob::Pattern::new(pattern) {\n319\t        Ok(glob_pattern) => {\n320\t            // The glob crate's Pattern::matches takes a &str directly\n321\t            if glob_pattern.matches(model_name) {\n322\t                Some(())\n323\t            } else {\n324\t                None\n325\t            }\n326\t        }\n327\t        Err(_) => {\n328\t            // Invalid glob pattern\n329\t            None\n330\t        }\n331\t    }\n332\t}\n333\t\n334\t/// Match a model name against a glob pattern.\n335\t///\n336\t/// This function uses the `glob` crate's Pattern functionality to perform\n337\t/// glob-style pattern matching against model names.\n338\t///\n339\t/// # Arguments\n340\t///\n341\t/// * `pattern` - Glob pattern to match (e.g., \"claude-*\", \"gpt-*\", \"*\").\n342\t/// * `model_name` - The model name to test against the pattern.\n343\t///\n344\t/// # Returns\n345\t///\n346\t/// * `true` - The pattern matches the model name.\n347\t/// * `false` - The pattern does not match, pattern is invalid, or either argument is empty.\n348\t///\n349\t/// # Glob Pattern Syntax\n350\t///\n351\t/// * `*` - Matches any sequence of non-separator characters.\n352\t/// * `**` - Matches any sequence of characters, including path separators.\n353\t/// * `?` - Matches any single non-separator character.\n354\t/// * `[a-z]` - Matches any character in the bracket.\n355\t/// * `[!a-z]` - Matches any character not in the bracket.\n356\t///\n357\t/// # Examples\n358\t///\n359\t/// ```\n360\t/// use needle::routing::match_glob;\n361\t///\n362\t/// // Match with wildcard\n363\t/// assert!(match_glob(\"claude-*\", \"claude-sonnet-4-6\"));\n364\t/// assert!(match_glob(\"claude-*\", \"claude-opus-4-6\"));\n365\t/// assert!(!match_glob(\"claude-*\", \"gpt-4\"));\n366\t///\n367\t/// // Match with double wildcard\n368\t/// assert!(match_glob(\"**\", \"any-model\"));\n369\t///\n370\t/// // Edge cases\n371\t/// assert!(!match_glob(\"\", \"model\"));  // Empty pattern\n372\t/// assert!(!match_glob(\"pattern\", \"\"));  // Empty model name\n373\t/// ```\n374\tpub fn match_glob(pattern: &str, model_name: &str) -> bool {\n375\t    // Handle edge cases\n376\t    if pattern.is_empty() || model_name.is_empty() {\n377\t        return false;\n378\t    }\n379\t\n380\t    // Use the glob crate to compile and match the pattern\n381\t    match glob::Pattern::new(pattern) {\n382\t        Ok(glob_pattern) => glob_pattern.matches(model_name),\n383\t        Err(_) => false, // Invalid glob pattern\n384\t    }\n385\t}\n386\t\n387\t// Routing rule matcher for model-to-adapter dispatch.\n//!\n//! Provides pattern matching logic for routing rules: regex/glob patterns\n//! against model names, first-match-wins semantics, and default fallback.\n\nuse crate::config::RoutingRule;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\n/// Compiled routing rule with cached regex for efficient matching.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\nstruct CompiledRule {\n    /// Compiled regex matcher.\n    matcher: Arc<regex::Regex>,\n    /// Adapter to use on match.\n    adapter: String,\n}\n\nimpl CompiledRule {\n    /// Compile a routing rule into an efficient matcher.\n    ///\n    /// Supports both regex patterns (any valid regex) and glob-style patterns:\n    /// - `*` matches any single path segment (non-greedy `[^/]+`)\n    /// - `**` matches zero or more path segments (`.+?` with greedy quantifier)\n    /// - Literal `*` or `**` must be escaped as `\\*` or `\\*\\*`\n    fn from_rule(rule: &RoutingRule) -> Result<Self, regex::Error> {\n        let pattern = &rule.match_model;\n        let adapter = rule.adapter.clone();\n\n        // Convert glob patterns to regex if needed.\n        // If the pattern contains * or ** without proper regex escaping,\n        // treat it as a glob pattern and convert.\n        let regex_pattern = if needs_glob_conversion(pattern) {\n            convert_glob_to_regex(pattern)\n        } else {\n            pattern.clone()\n        };\n\n        let matcher = regex::Regex::new(&regex_pattern)?;\n\n        Ok(CompiledRule {\n            matcher: Arc::new(matcher),\n            adapter,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Test if a model name matches this rule.\n    fn matches(&self, model: &str) -> bool {\n        self.matcher.is_match(model)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Check if a pattern is a glob pattern.\n///\n/// A simple heuristic that returns true if the pattern contains glob-style\n/// wildcards (`*` or `**`). This is a basic check that doesn't attempt to\n/// distinguish between glob and regex patterns - it just reports whether\n/// the pattern contains wildcard characters.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `pattern` - The pattern string to check.\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `true` if the pattern contains `*` or `**`.\n/// * `false` otherwise.\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::routing::is_glob_pattern;\n///\n/// // Glob patterns with wildcards\n/// assert!(is_glob_pattern(\"*\"));\n/// assert!(is_glob_pattern(\"**\"));\n/// assert!(is_glob_pattern(\"gpt-*\"));\n/// assert!(is_glob_pattern(\"test/**\"));\n///\n/// // Non-glob patterns (no wildcards)\n/// assert!(!is_glob_pattern(\"exact-match\"));\n/// assert!(!is_glob_pattern(\"gpt-4\"));\n/// assert!(!is_glob_pattern(\"claude-sonnet\"));\n/// ```\npub fn is_glob_pattern(pattern: &str) -> bool {\n    pattern.contains('*')\n}\n\n/// Check if a pattern contains glob-style wildcards that need conversion.\n///\n/// Returns true if the pattern appears to be a glob pattern rather than\n/// a well-formed regex. The heuristic checks for:\n/// 1. Regex features: anchors (^$), character classes [], parentheses (),\n///    quantifiers +?{}, alternation |, or the regex wildcard sequence .*\n/// 2. If present, it's a regex pattern - no conversion needed\n/// 3. If absent, but * is present, it's a glob pattern - convert it\nfn needs_glob_conversion(pattern: &str) -> bool {\n    // First, check if it looks like a regex by looking for regex metacharacters.\n    // The key indicator is .* which is \"any character\" in regex but not in glob.\n    let has_regex_features = pattern.contains(|c| {\n        matches!(\n            c,\n            '^' | '$' | '(' | ')' | '[' | ']' | '{' | '}' | '+' | '?' | '|' | '\\\\'\n        )\n    }) || pattern.contains(\".*\");\n\n    if has_regex_features {\n        // Has clear regex features - treat as regex\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    // At this point, we have a simple pattern that might be glob or regex.\n    // If it contains unescaped * (and we already ruled out other regex chars),\n    // treat it as a glob pattern.\n    let chars: Vec<char> = pattern.chars().collect();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < chars.len() {\n        if chars[i] == '\\\\' && i + 1 < chars.len() {\n            // Skip escaped character.\n            i += 2;\n            continue;\n        }\n        if chars[i] == '*' {\n            return true;\n        }\n        i += 1;\n    }\n\n    false\n}\n\n/// Convert glob-style pattern to regex.\n///\n/// Rules:\n/// - `*` alone → `.*` (match anything, catch-all)\n/// - `*` in other contexts → `[^/]+` (match any single segment, no slashes)\n/// - `**` → `.*` (match any characters including slashes, greedy)\n/// - Escaped `\\*` and `\\*\\*` treated literally\n/// - No implicit start anchor for glob patterns (unlike regex patterns)\nfn convert_glob_to_regex(glob: &str) -> String {\n    // Special case: * and ** should match anything (including empty).\n    if glob == \"*\" || glob == \"**\" {\n        return \"^.*$\".to_string();\n    }\n\n    let mut result = String::new();\n    let chars: Vec<char> = glob.chars().collect();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < chars.len() {\n        match chars[i] {\n            '\\\\' => {\n                // Escaped character - pass through the backslash and the character.\n                // This ensures that \\* in the glob becomes \\* in the regex (literal asterisk).\n                if i + 1 < chars.len() {\n                    result.push('\\\\');\n                    result.push(chars[i + 1]);\n                    i += 2;\n                } else {\n                    // Trailing backslash - treat literally.\n                    result.push('\\\\');\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            '*' => {\n                // Check for **.\n                if i + 1 < chars.len() && chars[i + 1] == '*' {\n                    // ** matches any characters including slashes.\n                    result.push_str(\".*\");\n                    i += 2;\n                } else {\n                    // * matches any non-slash characters.\n                    result.push_str(\"[^/]+\");\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            c => {\n                // Pass through regex metacharacters literally - regex::Regex::new\n                // will handle escaping. We only need to escape backslashes for\n                // the glob conversion.\n                result.push(c);\n                i += 1;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Only add end anchor, not start anchor (glob patterns match substrings).\n    format!(\"{}$\", result)\n}\n\n/// Match a model name against routing rules, returning the adapter to use.\n///\n/// Evaluates rules in order; the first matching rule determines the adapter.\n/// If no rule matches, returns the default adapter.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `model` - The model name to match (e.g., \"claude-sonnet-4-6\").\n/// * `rules` - Ordered list of routing rules (first match wins).\n/// * `default` - Fallback adapter when no rules match.\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Some(adapter)` - The adapter name to use.\n/// * `None` - No rule matched and default is empty/invalid (caller should handle).\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::routing::match_adapter;\n/// use needle::config::RoutingRule;\n///\n/// let rules = vec![\n///     RoutingRule {\n///         match_model: \"sonnet.*\".to_string(),\n///         adapter: \"claude-print\".to_string(),\n///     },\n///     RoutingRule {\n///         match_model: \"*\".to_string(),\n///         adapter: \"default-adapter\".to_string(),\n///     },\n/// ];\n///\n/// // First rule matches.\n/// assert_eq!(\n///     match_adapter(\"sonnet-4-6\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n///     Some(\"claude-print\".to_string())\n/// );\n///\n/// // Second rule (catch-all) matches.\n/// assert_eq!(\n///     match_adapter(\"other-model\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n///     Some(\"default-adapter\".to_string())\n/// );\n/// ```\npub fn match_adapter(model: &str, rules: &[RoutingRule], default: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    // Compile rules and test in order (first match wins).\n    for rule in rules {\n        match CompiledRule::from_rule(rule) {\n            Ok(compiled) => {\n                if compiled.matches(model) {\n                    return Some(compiled.adapter.clone());\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                // Log the error but continue with other rules.\n                // Invalid patterns are skipped rather than failing the entire dispatch.\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    pattern = %rule.match_model,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"invalid routing pattern — skipping rule\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // No rule matched — use default if provided.\n    if default.is_empty() {\n        None\n    } else {\n        Some(default.to_string())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Match a model name against a single glob pattern using the glob crate.\n///\n/// This is a lower-level function that tests if a glob pattern matches a model name.\n/// It uses the `glob` crate's Pattern type directly for glob-style pattern matching.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `pattern` - Glob pattern to match (e.g., \"claude-*\", \"gpt-*\", \"*\").\n/// * `model_name` - The model name to test against the pattern.\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Some(())` - The pattern matches the model name.\n/// * `None` - The pattern does not match or is invalid.\n///\n/// # Edge Cases\n///\n/// * Empty pattern: Returns `None` (no match).\n/// * Empty model name: Returns `None` (no match).\n/// * Invalid glob pattern: Returns `None` (no match).\n///\n/// # Glob Pattern Syntax\n///\n/// * `*` - Matches any sequence of non-separator characters.\n/// * `**` - Matches any sequence of characters, including path separators.\n/// * `?` - Matches any single non-separator character.\n/// * `[a-z]` - Matches any character in the bracket.\n/// * `[!a-z]` - Matches any character not in the bracket.\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::routing::match_adapter_with_glob;\n///\n/// // Match with wildcard\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"claude-sonnet-4-6\").is_some());\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"claude-opus-4-6\").is_some());\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"gpt-4\").is_none());\n///\n/// // Match with double wildcard\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"**\", \"any-model\").is_some());\n///\n/// // Edge cases\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"\", \"model\").is_none());\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"pattern\", \"\").is_none());\n/// ```\npub fn match_adapter_with_glob(pattern: &str, model_name: &str) -> Option<()> {\n    // Handle edge cases\n    if pattern.is_empty() || model_name.is_empty() {\n        return None;\n    }\n\n    // Use the glob crate to compile and match the pattern\n    match glob::Pattern::new(pattern) {\n        Ok(glob_pattern) => {\n            // The glob crate's Pattern::matches takes a &str directly\n            if glob_pattern.matches(model_name) {\n                Some(())\n            } else {\n                None\n            }\n        }\n        Err(_) => {\n            // Invalid glob pattern\n            None\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Match a model name against a glob pattern.\n///\n/// This function uses the `glob` crate's Pattern functionality to perform\n/// glob-style pattern matching against model names.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `pattern` - Glob pattern to match (e.g., \"claude-*\", \"gpt-*\", \"*\").\n/// * `model_name` - The model name to test against the pattern.\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `true` - The pattern matches the model name.\n/// * `false` - The pattern does not match, pattern is invalid, or either argument is empty.\n///\n/// # Glob Pattern Syntax\n///\n/// * `*` - Matches any sequence of non-separator characters.\n/// * `**` - Matches any sequence of characters, including path separators.\n/// * `?` - Matches any single non-separator character.\n/// * `[a-z]` - Matches any character in the bracket.\n/// * `[!a-z]` - Matches any character not in the bracket.\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::routing::match_glob;\n///\n/// // Match with wildcard\n/// assert!(match_glob(\"claude-*\", \"claude-sonnet-4-6\"));\n/// assert!(match_glob(\"claude-*\", \"claude-opus-4-6\"));\n/// assert!(!match_glob(\"claude-*\", \"gpt-4\"));\n///\n/// // Match with double wildcard\n/// assert!(match_glob(\"**\", \"any-model\"));\n///\n/// // Edge cases\n/// assert!(!match_glob(\"\", \"model\"));  // Empty pattern\n/// assert!(!match_glob(\"pattern\", \"\"));  // Empty model name\n/// ```\npub fn match_glob(pattern: &str, model_name: &str) -> bool {\n    // Handle edge cases\n    if pattern.is_empty() || model_name.is_empty() {\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    // Use the glob crate to compile and match the pattern\n    match glob::Pattern::new(pattern) {\n        Ok(glob_pattern) => glob_pattern.matches(model_name),\n        Err(_) => false, // Invalid glob pattern\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Tests\n// match_adapter(\"gpt-4\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n            Some(\"fallback\".to_string())\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn non_matching_regex_patterns() {\n        // Test that non-matching patterns correctly return default.\n        let rules = vec![make_rule(\"^gpt-4$\", \"exact-adapter\")];\n\n        // Exact match works.\n        assert_eq!(\n            match_adapter(\"gpt-4\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n            Some(\"exact-adapter\".to_string())\n        );\n\n        // Non-matching models fall back to default.\n        assert_eq!(\n            match_adapter(\"gpt-3.5\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n            Some(\"fallback\".to_string())\n        );\n        assert_eq!(\n            match_adapter(\"gpt-4-turbo\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n            Some(\"fallback\".to_string())\n        );\n        assert_eq!(\n            match_adapter(\"claude-sonnet\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n            Some(\"fallback\".to_string())\n        );\n    }\n\n ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Where a configuration value originated.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum ConfigSource {\n    /// Built-in default value.\n    Default,\n    /// Global config file (`~/.config/needle/config.yaml`).\n    GlobalFile(PathBuf),\n    /// Workspace config file (`.needle.yaml`).\n    WorkspaceFile(PathBuf),\n    /// Environment variable override.\n    EnvVar(String),\n    /// CLI argument override.\n    CliOverride,\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for ConfigSource {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            ConfigSource::Default => write!(f, \"built-in default\"),\n            ConfigSource::GlobalFile(p) => write!(f, \"{}\", p.display()),\n            ConfigSource::WorkspaceFile(p) => write!(f, \"{}\", p.display()),\n            ConfigSource::EnvVar(name) => write!(f, \"{} env var\", name),\n            ConfigSource::CliOverride => write!(f, \"CLI argument\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Map of config field paths to their source.\n///\n/// Used by `needle config --dump --show-source` to annotate each value.\npub type SourceMap = BTreeMap<String, ConfigSource>;\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Workspace Overrides\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Subset of configuration that can be overridden per-workspace via `.needle.yaml`.\n///\n/// Only these sections are allowed at the workspace level:\n/// - `agent.default`, `agent.timeout`\n/// - `strands` (weave, pulse, unravel)\n/// - `prompt.*`\n/// - `verification` (legacy) or `gates` (new pluggable system)\n///\n/// Non-overridable sections (worker, limits, health, telemetry) are detected\n/// and produce warnings.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Deserialize)]\npub struct WorkspaceOverrides {\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub agent: Option<WorkspaceAgentOverrides>,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub strands: Option<WorkspaceStrandsOverrides>,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub prompt: Option<PromptConfig>,\n    /// Verification commands run after agent success, before accepting closure.\n    /// Legacy format — prefer `gates` for new configurations.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub verification: Option<Vec<String>>,\n    /// Pluggable validation gates.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub gates: Option<Vec<GateConfig>>,\n    /// Workspace identity labels (overridable per-workspace).\n    ///\n    /// Set in `.needle.yaml` under `workspace.labels`. Used for cross-workspace\n    /// skill sharing: skills from Explore workspaces whose labels overlap with\n    /// these labels are injected into prompts alongside local skills.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub workspace: Option<WorkspaceLabelsOverride>,\n}\n\n/// Agent fields overridable at the workspace level.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]\npub struct WorkspaceAgentOverrides {\n    pub default: Option<String>,\n    pub timeout: Option<u64>,\n    pub routing: Option<RoutingConfig>,\n}\n\n/// Strand fields overridable at the workspace level.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Deserialize)]\npub struct WorkspaceStrandsOverrides {\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub weave: Option<serde_yaml::Value>,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub pulse: Option<serde_yaml::Value>,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub unravel: Option<serde_yaml::Value>,\n}\n\n/// Non-overridable top-level keys in workspace config.\n///\n/// Note: `workspace` is intentionally absent — `workspace.labels` IS overridable\n/// per-workspace. The path fields (`default`, `home`) are simply ignored if set.\nconst NON_OVERRIDABLE_KEYS: &[&str] = &[\"worker\", \"limits\", \"health\", \"telemetry\"];\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Top-level Config\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Fully resolved NEEDLE configuration.\n///\n/// Loaded once at boot, immutable during a session.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct Config {\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub agent: AgentConfig,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub worker: WorkerConfig,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub workspace: WorkspaceConfig,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub strands: StrandsConfig,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub telemetry: TelemetryConfig,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub prompt: PromptConfig,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub health: HealthConfig,\n    /// Provider/model concurrency and rate limits.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub limits: LimitsConfig,\n    /// Per-model token pricing (USD per million tokens).\n    #[serde(default = \"crate::cost::default_pricing\")]\n    pub pricing: PricingConfig,\n    /// Daily budget thresholds for cost enforcement.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub budget: BudgetConfig,\n    /// Verification commands run after agent success, before accepting closure.\n    /// Legacy format — prefer `gates` for new configurations.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub verification: Vec<String>,\n    /// Pluggable validation gates.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub gates: Vec<GateConfig>,\n    /// Self-modification (hot-reload) configuration.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub self_modification: SelfModificationConfig,\n    /// FABRIC live dashboard forwarding.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub fabric: FabricConfig,\n    /// Supervisor detection configuration.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub supervisor: SupervisorConfig,\n}\n\nimpl Config {\n    /// Expand all tilde (~) paths to absolute paths using $HOME.\n    ///\n    /// This must be called after deserialization to ensure all paths\n    /// like `~/.needle` are expanded to `/home/user/.needle`.\n    /// Paths without tildes are left unchanged.\n    pub fn expand_tildes(&mut self) {\n        // workspace section\n        self.workspace.default = expand_tilde(&self.workspace.default);\n        self.workspace.home = expand_tilde(&self.workspace.home);\n\n        // agent section\n        self.agent.adapters_dir = expand_tilde(&self.agent.adapters_dir);\n\n        // strands.explore section\n        self.strands.explore.workspace_root = expand_tilde(&self.strands.explore.workspace_root);\n        self.strands.explore.workspaces = expand_tilde_vec(&self.strands.explore.workspaces);\n\n        // strands.weave section\n        self.strands.weave.exclude_workspaces =\n            expand_tilde_vec(&self.strands.weave.exclude_workspaces);\n\n        // strands.splice section\n        self.strands.splice.report_workspace =\n            expand_tilde_option(&self.strands.splice.report_workspace);\n\n        // strands.pulse.scanners[].command paths are strings, not PathBuf, so skip\n\n        // strands.reflect section - no PathBuf fields\n\n        // strands.learning section\n        self.strands.learning.global_learnings_file =\n            expand_tilde(&self.strands.learning.global_learnings_file);\n\n        // telemetry section\n        if let Some(ref mut log_dir) = self.telemetry.file_sink.log_dir {\n            *log_dir = expand_tilde(log_dir);\n        }\n\n        // health section\n        self.health.heartbeat_dir = expand_tilde_option(&self.health.heartbeat_dir);\n\n        // supervisor section\n        self.supervisor.heartbeat_path = expand_tilde_option(&self.supervisor.heartbeat_path);\n        self.supervisor.socket_path = expand_tilde_option(&self.supervisor.socket_path);\n\n        // prompt section\n        self.prompt.context_files = expand_tilde_vec(&self.prompt.context_files);\n\n        // self_modification section\n        self.self_modification.canary_workspace =\n            expand_tilde(&self.self_modification.canary_workspace);\n\n        // prompt.variants[].content_file\n        for variants in self.prompt.variants.values_mut() {\n            for variant in variants {\n                variant.content_file = expand_tilde(&variant.content_file);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Config validation\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A single config validation error.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct ConfigError {\n    /// Dot-separated field path (e.g., `agent.default`).\n    pub field: String,\n    /// Human-readable explanation.\n    pub message: String,\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for ConfigError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        write!(f, \"{}: {}\", self.field, self.message)\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// CLI overrides\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// CLI-level overrides applied after all file-based config loading.\n#[derive(Debug, Default)]\npub struct CliOverrides {\n    pub workspace: Option<PathBuf>,\n    pub worker_name: Option<String>,\n    pub agent_binary: Option<String>,\n    pub max_workers: Option<u32>,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ConfigLoader\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Loads and validates NEEDLE configuration.\npub struct ConfigLoader;\n\nimpl ConfigLoader {\n    /// Load global config from `~/.config/needle/config.yaml`.\n    ///\n    /// If the file does not exist, returns the default config (not an error).\n    pub fn load_global() -> Result<Config> {\n        let path = dirs_or_home(\".config/needle/config.yaml\");\n        Self::load_from_path(&path)\n    }\n\n    /// Load config from a specific path.\n    ///\n    /// If the file does not exist, returns the default config.\n    pub fn load_from_path(path: &Path) -> Result<Config> {\n        if !path.exists() {\n            let mut config = Config::default();\n            config.expand_tildes();\n            return Ok(config);\n        }\n        let text = std::fs::read_to_string(path)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read config file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n        let mut config: Config = serde_yaml::from_str(&text)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid YAML in config file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n        config.expand_tildes();\n        Ok(config)\n    }\n\n    /// Load workspace overrides from `.needle.yaml` in the given workspace root.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `None` if the file does not exist. Emits warnings for\n    /// non-overridable keys found in the workspace config.\n    pub fn load_workspace(workspace_root: &Path) -> Result<Option<WorkspaceOverrides>> {\n        let path = workspace_root.join(\".needle.yaml\");\n        if !path.exists() {\n            return Ok(None);\n        }\n        let text = std::fs::read_to_string(&path)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read workspace config: {}\", path.display()))?;\n\n        // Check for non-overridable keys and warn.\n        Self::warn_non_overridable_keys(&text, &path)?;\n\n        let overrides: WorkspaceOverrides = serde_yaml::from_str(&text)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid YAML in workspace config: {}\", path.display()))?;\n        Ok(Some(overrides))\n    }\n\n    /// Warn about non-overridable top-level keys in workspace config YAML.\n    fn warn_non_overridable_keys(yaml_text: &str, path: &Path) -> Result<()> {\n        let value: serde_yaml::Value = serde_yaml::from_str(yaml_text)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid YAML in workspace config: {}\", path.display()))?;\n\n        if let serde_yaml::Value::Mapping(map) = value {\n            for key in map.keys() {\n                if let serde_yaml::Value::String(key_str) = key {\n                    if NON_OVERRIDABLE_KEYS.contains(&key_str.as_str()) {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            key = %key_str,\n                            path = %path.display(),\n                            \"workspace config contains non-overridable setting '{}' — ignored\",\n                            key_str,\n                        );\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Apply workspace overrides to a config.\n    ///\n    /// Only overridable fields are applied. Records sources in the source map.\n    pub fn apply_workspace(\n        config: &mut Config,\n        overrides: &WorkspaceOverrides,\n        ws_path: &Path,\n        sources: &mut SourceMap,\n    ) {\n        let source = ConfigSource::WorkspaceFile(ws_path.join(\".needle.yaml\"));\n\n        if let Some(ref agent) = overrides.agent {\n            if let Some(ref default) = agent.default {\n                config.agent.default = default.clone();\n                sources.insert(\"agent.default\".to_string(), source.clone());\n            }\n            if let Some(timeout) = agent.timeout {\n                config.agent.timeout = timeout;\n                sources.insert(\"agent.timeout\".to_string(), source.clone());\n            }\n            if let Some(ref routing) = agent.routing {\n                config.agent.routing = Some(routing.clone());\n                sources.insert(\"agent.routing\".to_string(), source.clone());\n            }\n        }\n\n        if let Some(ref strands) = overrides.strands {\n            if let Some(ref weave_val) = strands.weave {\n                if let Ok(weave_cfg) = serde_yaml::from_value::<WeaveConfig>(weave_val.clone()) {\n                    config.strands.weave = weave_cfg;\n                }\n                sources.insert(\"strands.weave\".to_string(), source.clone());\n            }\n            if let Some(ref pulse_val) = strands.pulse {\n                if let Ok(pulse_cfg) = serde_yaml::from_value::<PulseConfig>(pulse_val.clone()) {\n                    config.strands.pulse = pulse_cfg;\n                }\n                sources.insert(\"strands.pulse\".to_string(), source.clone());\n            }\n            if let Some(ref unravel_val) = strands.unravel {\n                if let Ok(unravel_cfg) =\n                    serde_yaml::from_value::<UnravelConfig>(unravel_val.clone())\n                {\n                    config.strands.unravel = unravel_cfg;\n                }\n                sources.insert(\"strands.unravel\".to_string(), source.clone());\n            }\n        }\n\n        if let Some(ref prompt) = overrides.prompt {\n            config.prompt = prompt.clone();\n            sources.insert(\"prompt.context_files\".to_string(), source.clone());\n            sources.insert(\"prompt.instructions\".to_string(), source.clone());\n        }\n\n        if let Some(ref verification) = overrides.verification {\n            config.verification = verification.clone();\n            sources.insert(\"verification\".to_string(), source.clone());\n        }\n\n        if let Some(ref gates) = overrides.gates {\n            config.gates = gates.clone();\n            sources.insert(\"gates\".to_string(), source.clone());\n        }\n\n        if let Some(ref ws) = overrides.workspace {\n            if !ws.labels.is_empty() {\n                config.workspace.labels = ws.labels.clone();\n                sources.insert(\"workspace.labels\".to_string(), source);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Apply environment variable overrides (`NEEDLE_*` prefix, `__` separator).\n    ///\n    /// Example: `NEEDLE_AGENT__DEFAULT=opus` sets `agent.default` to `\"opus\"`.\n    pub fn apply_env_overrides(config: &mut Config, sources: &mut SourceMap) {\n        for (key, value) in std::env::vars() {\n            if let Some(suffix) = key.strip_prefix(\"NEEDLE_\") {\n                let config_path = suffix.to_lowercase().replace(\"__\", \".\");\n                let source = ConfigSource::EnvVar(key.clone());\n\n                match config_path.as_str() {\n                    \"agent.default\" => {\n                        config.agent.default = value;\n                        sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                    }\n                    \"agent.timeout\" => {\n                        if let Ok(v) = value.parse::<u64>() {\n                            config.agent.timeout = v;\n                            sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                        } else {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                env_var = %key,\n                                value = %value,\n                                \"invalid value for agent.timeout — expected integer\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                    }\n                    \"agent.routing.default_adapter\" => {\n                        config\n                            .agent\n                            .routing\n                            .get_or_insert_with(RoutingConfig::default)\n                            .default_adapter = Some(value);\n                        sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                    }\n                    \"worker.max_workers\" => {\n                        if let Ok(v) = value.parse::<u32>() {\n                            config.worker.max_workers = v;\n                            sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                        } else {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                env_var = %key,\n                                value = %value,\n                                \"invalid value for worker.max_workers — expected integer\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                    }\n                    \"worker.idle_timeout\" => {\n                        if let Ok(v) = value.parse::<u64>() {\n                            config.worker.idle_timeout = v;\n                            sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                        } else {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                env_var = %key,\n                                value = %value,\n                                \"invalid value for worker.idle_timeout — expected integer\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                    }\n                    \"worker.launch_stagger_seconds\" => {\n                        if let Ok(v) = value.parse::<u64>() {\n                            config.worker.launch_stagger_seconds = v;\n                            sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                        } else {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                env_var = %key,\n                                value = %value,\n                                \"invalid value for worker.launch_stagger_seconds — expected integer\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                    }\n                    \"health.heartbeat_interval_secs\" => {\n                        if let Ok(v) = value.parse::<u64>() {\n                            config.health.heartbeat_interval_secs = v;\n                            sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                        } else {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                env_var = %key,\n                                value = %value,\n                                \"invalid value for health.heartbeat_interval_secs — expected integer\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                    }\n                    \"health.heartbeat_ttl_secs\" => {\n                        if let Ok(v) = value.parse::<u64>() {\n                            config.health.heartbeat_ttl_secs = v;\n                            sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                        } else {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                env_var = %key,\n                                value = %value,\n                                \"invalid value for health.heartbeat_ttl_secs — expected integer\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                    }\n                    \"self_modification.enabled\" => {\n                        if let Ok(v) = value.parse::<bool>() {\n                            config.self_modification.enabled = v;\n                            sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                        } else {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                env_var = %key,\n                                value = %value,\n                                \"invalid value for self_modification.enabled — expected true/false\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                    }\n                    \"self_modification.auto_promote\" => {\n                        if let Ok(v) = value.parse::<bool>() {\n                            config.self_modification.auto_promote = v;\n                            sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                        } else {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                env_var = %key,\n                                value = %value,\n                                \"invalid value for self_modification.auto_promote — expected true/false\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                    }\n                    \"self_modification.canary_timeout\" => {\n                        if let Ok(v) = value.parse::<u64>() {\n                            config.self_modification.canary_timeout = v;\n                            sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                        } else {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                env_var = %key,\n                                value = %value,\n                                \"invalid value for self_modification.canary_timeout — expected integer\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                    }\n                    \"supervisor.heartbeat_path\" => {\n                        config.supervisor.heartbeat_path =\n                            Some(expand_tilde(&PathBuf::from(value)));\n                        sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                    }\n                    \"supervisor.socket_path\" => {\n                        config.supervisor.socket_path = Some(expand_tilde(&PathBuf::from(value)));\n                        sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                    }\n                    \"workspace.home\" => {\n                        config.workspace.home = expand_tilde(&PathBuf::from(value));\n                        sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                    }\n                    \"workspace.default\" => {\n                        config.workspace.default = expand_tilde(&PathBuf::from(value));\n                        sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                    }\n                    _ => {\n                        tracing::debug!(\n                            env_var = %key,\n                            config_path = %config_path,\n                            \"unrecognized NEEDLE_ environment variable — ignored\"\n                        );\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Apply CLI overrides (highest precedence) to a loaded config.\n    pub fn apply_overrides(config: &mut Config, overrides: CliOverrides) {\n        Self::apply_cli_overrides(config, overrides, &mut SourceMap::new());\n    }\n\n    /// Apply CLI overrides with source tracking.\n    pub fn apply_cli_overrides(\n        config: &mut Config,\n        overrides: CliOverrides,\n        sources: &mut SourceMap,\n    ) {\n        if let Some(ws) = overrides.workspace {\n            config.workspace.default = ws;\n            sources.insert(\"workspace.default\".to_string(), ConfigSource::CliOverride);\n        }\n        if let Some(agent) = overrides.agent_binary {\n            config.agent.default = agent;\n            sources.insert(\"agent.default\".to_string(), ConfigSource::CliOverride);\n        }\n        if let Some(n) = overrides.max_workers {\n            config.worker.max_workers = n;\n            sources.insert(\"worker.max_workers\".to_string(), ConfigSource::CliOverride);\n        }\n        // worker_name is handled at the Worker level, not stored in Config\n    }\n\n    /// Load the fully resolved configuration using the complete hierarchy:\n    ///\n    /// defaults → global file → workspace `.needle.yaml` → env vars → CLI args\n    ///\n    /// Returns the resolved config and a source map showing where each value\n    /// came from. The source map only contains entries for values that were\n    /// overridden from their defaults.\n    pub fn load_resolved(workspace_root: &Path, cli: CliOverrides) -> Result<(Config, SourceMap)> {\n        let mut sources = SourceMap::new();\n\n        // Layer 1 + 2: defaults + global config.\n        let global_path = dirs_or_home(\".config/needle/config.yaml\");\n        let mut config = Self::load_from_path(&global_path)?;\n\n        // Track which fields came from global config (if file existed).\n        if global_path.exists() {\n            let source = ConfigSource::GlobalFile(global_path);\n            // Mark all top-level sections as from global.\n            for key in &[\n                \"agent.default\",\n                \"agent.timeout\",\n                \"worker.max_workers\",\n                \"worker.idle_timeout\",\n                \"health.heartbeat_interval_secs\",\n                \"health.heartbeat_ttl_secs\",\n            ] {\n                sources.insert((*key).to_string(), source.clone());\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Layer 3: workspace config.\n        if let Some(ws_overrides) = Self::load_workspace(workspace_root)? {\n            Self::apply_workspace(&mut config, &ws_overrides, workspace_root, &mut sources);\n        }\n\n        // Layer 4: environment variables.\n        Self::apply_env_overrides(&mut config, &mut sources);\n\n        // Layer 5: CLI arguments.\n        Self::apply_cli_overrides(&mut config, cli, &mut sources);\n\n        // Expand all tildes after all overrides are applied.\n        config.expand_tildes();\n\n        Ok((config, sources))\n    }\n\n    /// Validate a resolved config.\n    ///\n    /// Returns a list of errors (empty = valid).\n    pub fn validate(config: &Config) -> Vec<ConfigError> {\n        let mut errors = Vec::new();\n\n        if config.agent.default.is_empty() {\n            errors.push(ConfigError {\n                field: \"agent.default\".to_string(),\n                message: \"must not be empty\".to_string(),\n            });\n        }\n\n        if config.worker.max_workers == 0 {\n            errors.push(ConfigError {\n                field: \"worker.max_workers\".to_string(),\n                message: \"must be at least 1\".to_string(),\n            });\n        }\n\n        if config.worker.max_workers > 50 {\n            errors.push(ConfigError {\n                field: \"worker.max_workers\".to_string(),\n                message: format!(\n                    \"{} exceeds practical fleet limit of 50\",\n                    config.worker.max_workers\n                ),\n            });\n        }\n\n        if config.worker.cpu_load_warn <= 0.0 || config.worker.cpu_load_warn > 1.0 {\n            errors.push(ConfigError {\n                field: \"worker.cpu_load_warn\".to_string(),\n                message: \"must be in range (0.0, 1.0]\".to_string(),\n            });\n        }\n\n        if config.health.heartbeat_ttl_secs < 3 * config.health.heartbeat_interval_secs {\n            errors.push(ConfigError {\n                field: \"health.heartbeat_ttl_secs\".to_string(),\n                message: format!(\n                    \"should be >= 3 * heartbeat_interval_secs ({}); detection may be unreliable\",\n                    3 * config.health.heartbeat_interval_secs\n                ),\n            });\n        }\n\n        // Validate routing regex patterns.\n        if let Some(ref routing) = config.agent.routing {\n            for (idx, rule) in routing.rules.iter().enumerate() {\n                // Validate that match_model is a valid regex.\n                if let Err(e) = regex::Regex::new(&rule.match_model) {\n                    errors.push(ConfigError {\n                        field: format!(\"agent.routing.rules[{}].match_model\", idx),\n                        message: format!(\"invalid regex pattern '{}': {}\", rule.match_model, e),\n                    });\n                }\n                // Validate that adapter is not empty.\n                if rule.adapter.is_empty() {\n                    errors.push(ConfigError {\n                        field: format!(\"agent.routing.rules[{}].adapter\", idx),\n                        message: \"must not be empty\".to_string(),\n                    });\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        errors\n    }\n\n    /// Format config values with source annotations for `--dump --show-source`.\n    pub fn dump_with_sources(config: &Config, sources: &SourceMap) -> Vec<String> {\n        let fields: Vec<(&str, String)> = vec![\n            (\"agent.default\", config.agent.default.clone()),\n            (\"agent.timeout\", config.agent.timeout.to_string()),\n            (\"worker.max_workers\", config.worker.max_workers.to_string()),\n            (\n                \"worker.idle_timeout\",\n                config.worker.idle_timeout.to_string(),\n            ),\n            (\n                \"worker.launch_stagger_seconds\",\n                config.worker.launch_stagger_seconds.to_string(),\n            ),\n            (\n                \"health.heartbeat_interval_secs\",\n                config.health.heartbeat_interval_secs.to_string(),\n            ),\n            (\n                \"health.heartbeat_ttl_secs\",\n                config.health.heartbeat_ttl_secs.to_string(),\n            ),\n            (\n                \"prompt.context_files\",\n                format!(\"{:?}\", config.prompt.context_files),\n            ),\n            (\n                \"prompt.instructions\",\n                config\n                    .prompt\n                    .instructions\n                    .as_deref()\n                    .unwrap_or(\"\")\n
